newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Wiesenthal praises Nuremberg 50 years on.
newsitem.headline: Wiesenthal praises Nuremberg 50 years on.

text.p: Veteran Nazi-hunter Simon Wiesenthal paid tribute to the Nuremberg trials on Tuesday, 50 years after allied judges pronounced landmark verdicts against key figures in Adolf Hitler's Nazi regime.
"Nuremberg was a just tribunal which...gave a fair hearing to the accused," Austrian news agency APA quoted Wiesenthal as saying.

The post-World War Two trials, which passed judgment on senior Nazis including Luftwaffe commander Hermann Goering, became a model for the present United Nations war crimes tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, Wiesenthal said.
But the threat of Soviet expansion in central and eastern Europe after 1947 initially checked the progress made at Nuremberg and allowed hundreds of Nazis to flee Europe, he said.
Wiesenthal, 87, who says he helped bring more than 1,000 escaped Nazis to book in a career spanning 50 years, is a survivor of the Holocaust.

He was absent from the start of the Nuremberg trials in November 1945 because he was recovering from emaciation after his liberation by U.S. soldiers from Mauthausen concentration camp, west of Vienna.
Once he was well enough, he travelled to Nuremberg and began poring over 110,000 tonnes of German documents in the hope of uncovering evidence to track down more Nazi suspects.
